title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 4
paragraphs: Of these, I have already spoken of the practices of the Getae, who believe themselves to be immortal. The Trausi perform everything else in the same manner as the other Thracians, but in regard to those who are born and die among them they do as follows. When a child has been born, the nearest relatives sit around it and lament for all the evils whose measure he must now fill, since he has been born, enumerating the whole range of human ills; but when a man dies, they cover him up in the earth with sport and rejoicing, saying at the same time from how great evils he has escaped and that he is now in perfect bliss.
